notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text:
Willie Klocko, 59M, here for follow-up of CKD and diabetes. Wife came with him.

S: Reports about three weeks of fatigue, poor appetite, and nausea most mornings, no vomiting. Some metallic taste. Ankles a bit puffier at the end of the day, uses furosemide about every other day now. No chest pain or shortness of breath at rest. Urinating a normal amount.
Knees still bothering him. On further questioning he has been taking naproxen 500 mg twice a day most days since around April, over the counter, because "the Tylenol didn't do anything." Was not aware this was a problem for his kidneys.
Still on metformin 500 mg twice daily, insulin 70/30, lisinopril 10 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, amlodipine 2.5 mg, metoprolol succinate 100 mg, clopidogrel, simvastatin. No missed doses.
Blood sugars at home 70-110, two readings in the 60s this month.

O: BP 84/52 sitting, HR 72. Wt 79.0 kg. Alert, looks tired. Lungs clear. No JVD. 1+ bilateral pitting edema to the ankles. Abdomen soft.
Most recent labs (8/19): creatinine 5.7, up from 3.69 in May and 4.4 in late July. eGFR 15.6. K 4.2. BUN 17. Glucose 91. Urine albumin/creatinine 179 mg/g.

A/P:
1. CKD progressing. Creatinine has climbed steadily since the spring and eGFR is now under 20. Symptoms today (fatigue, nausea, dysgeusia) may be uremic. Repeat BMP, CBC, phosphorus today. Urgent nephrology referral placed.
2. Daily NSAID use since April, previously unknown to us. Counseled to stop naproxen today. Will review the rest of the medication list against current kidney function once labs are back.
3. Type 2 diabetes. Running low at home. Reduce evening 70/30 insulin by 4 units. Metformin discussed, decision pending labs and nephrology input.
4. Chronic CHF with worsening edema. Continue furosemide as needed; reassess after labs.
5. Hypertension. Hypotensive on three agents. Hold HCTZ starting today.
6. Bilateral knee osteoarthritis. Topical diclofenac not appropriate either; discussed physical therapy referral.

Labs today, phone follow-up in 48 hours, RTC 1 week.

notes.author: Dr. Chen
notes.text:
Willie Klocko, 59M. Routine follow-up for diabetes, CKD and heart failure.

S: Feels "about the same." Energy a little low. Home BP cuff readings running in the 80s over 50s, no dizziness or falls. No chest pain, no orthopnea, sleeping on one pillow. Weight stable at home. Blood sugars mostly 90-140 fasting on the 70/30 insulin, one low of 62 last week after skipping lunch.
Both knees have been aching for a couple of months, worse after his shift. He takes Aleve from the pharmacy when it's bad, maybe a few times a week. No swelling, no locking. Denies any other new OTC or herbal products.
Still taking metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals, lisinopril, HCTZ, amlodipine, metoprolol, clopidogrel, simvastatin. Uses furosemide 40 mg only when his ankles swell, maybe once a week.

O: BP 80/48, HR 68, wt 79.0 kg (unchanged). Lungs clear. No JVD. Trace bilateral ankle edema. Knees: mild crepitus bilaterally, no effusion, full ROM.
Labs today: creatinine 3.69, down from 5.57 in April. eGFR 24. K 4.73. BUN 17.9. Glucose 84. Urine albumin/creatinine 123 mg/g. A1c reviewed.

A/P:
1. CKD, diabetic kidney disease. Creatinine improved this month but eGFR still in the 20s. Continue to follow monthly. Advised to avoid dehydration.
2. Type 2 diabetes on insulin 70/30 and metformin. Control acceptable. Reviewed hypoglycemia precautions.
3. Chronic CHF, NYHA II, euvolemic today. Continue metoprolol, lisinopril; furosemide prn. Home monitoring continues.
4. Hypertension. Home and office readings low; asked him to hold HCTZ if systolic under 85 and to let us know. No changes today.
5. Bilateral knee pain, likely osteoarthritis. Discussed acetaminophen as first line. Will address further at next visit.

RTC 4 weeks with BMP, sooner if symptoms.
